questions.q: What is a logical backup in MySQL, per this lesson?
options: A backup stored as SQL statements (like CREATE TABLE and INSERT) that is restored by re-executing them
A raw byte-for-byte copy of the InnoDB tablespace files
A backup that only captures table names with no data
A snapshot taken by the operating system's disk driver
questions.explain: A logical backup, produced by tools like mysqldump, dumps the logical structure and content as SQL text that is replayed to restore.

questions.q: What is a physical backup in MySQL, per this lesson?
options: A copy of the actual database files on disk, restored by putting the files back and starting the server
A printout of the database schema
A backup that only works for MyISAM tables
Another name for mysqldump
questions.explain: A physical backup copies raw data files (tablespaces, logs) directly; restoring means placing them back, with no SQL replay.

questions.q: Why does mysqldump restore time scale poorly for very large databases, per this lesson?
options: Restoring means re-executing SQL statements to rebuild every table and row from scratch
mysqldump only supports databases under 1 GB
mysqldump backups cannot be restored at all
mysqldump requires manual editing of every INSERT statement before restore
questions.explain: Because a logical restore replays SQL to rebuild data, restore time grows with data volume, unlike a physical restore.

questions.q: Why does MySQL's lack of a built-in tool for physical backups matter, per this lesson?
options: It's exactly why a specialized third-party physical backup tool becomes essential for large databases
It means physical backups are impossible in MySQL
It means MySQL databases can never exceed a small size
It means logical backups are always faster than physical ones
questions.explain: Unlike SQL Server, MySQL ships no built-in hot physical backup tool, which is exactly the gap a dedicated tool fills, as the next lesson covers.

questions.q: Per this lesson's rule of thumb, when is a logical backup (mysqldump) the better fit?
options: Smaller databases, migrations across versions or platforms, and human-readable snapshots
Multi-terabyte databases needing restores in minutes
Databases where restore speed is the only requirement that matters
Only when the database has no indexes
questions.explain: Logical backups shine for portability and smaller data volumes; physical backups win once size or restore-time requirements make SQL replay impractical.
